The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus directing respondents No. 2 &
4 to consider the claim of the petitioners under the land pooling scheme in terms of the policy
decision taken by the Board of Directors in 256th meeting dated 24.06.2022 at item No. 256/51 and
decide their representation dated 05.01.2024 along with reminder dated 12.02.2024 and to allot
25% developed land of residential use or 12.5% developed commercial plot to each of the petitioners
in proportion to their acquired land.

2.  It is not in dispute that the land of the petitioners was acquired by the respondent, Parishad, for public purpose under the provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam,
1965.

sentences.text: However, despite expiry of more than ten years, no award was declared.

The petitioners,
therefore, filed Writ-C No. 18402 of 2020.
During pendency of the writ petition

, petitioners No. 2 &
3, therein, transferred their land in favour of the Parishad by executing sale-deeds and therefore, the writ petition in respect of the aforesaid petitioners was dismissed as infructuous.

In respect of the other petitioners and certain other persons, who are now before this Court, the petition was disposed of by order dated 14.03.2023 with the following direction:-
"Considering the prayer made in the writ petition and the stand of U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad that they are agreeable to pay compensation to the petitioners for the acquired land as per the prevailing rules in the year 2016, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioners are at liberty to accept the rates fixed by the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad and in case of any denial on the part of the petitioners to enter into an agreement with the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, it would be incumbent upon the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer asking him to determine the compensation, strictly in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text:
In any case, the proceeding for determination of compensation for the acquired land by consent or by making an award by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, in accordance with the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, shall be completed within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order."
3.

In terms of the aforesaid order, another petition bearing Writ-C No. 14542 of 2023 filed by Harishankar (petitioner in Writ-C No. 8420 of 2024) was also disposed of by order dated 03.08.2023.
4.
The Parishad, it appears, had requested the Special Land Acquisition Officer to declare award in compliance of the order dated 14.03.2023 and similar orders passed in other matters.

sentences.text: While the aforesaid proceedings were pending, it seems that the petitioners moved application before the Parishad for extending the benefit of land pooling policy of the Parishad to the petitioners.

Under the said policy, the tenure holders, whose lands had been acquired, are entitled to 25% developed residential plot or 12.5% developed commercial plot in proportion to the area of the acquired land.
The said application filed by the petitioners dated 05.01.2024 and 12.02.2024 having not been considered, the instant petition has been filed.
6. Shri Nipun Singh, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent, Parishad, is in receipt of written instructions and the same is taken on record.

7. According to it, the Parishad has already written to the Special Land Acquisition Officer/Collector vide letter dated 10.08.2023 to declare award in compliance of the directions issued by this Court.
The stand taken is that the said proceedings are at advanced stage and Special Land Acquisition Officer is likely to declare the award within a short period.
8. In respect of land pooling policy, the stand taken is that the benefit thereof was extended to those persons who had applied.
Since the petitioners had not applied in the year 2022, but preferred the earlier writ, therefore, their claim under the said policy has not been considered.
In respect of the petitioners, the Special Land Acquisition Officer would be declaring the award and to which they would be entitled in terms of the orders of this Court.

In other words, the contention is that in view of the directions issued by this Court in the previous writ petitions, the Parishad is not bound to consider the claim of the petitioners under the land pooling policy.

9. We find that there is no bar under the land pooling policy nor even in terms of the directions issued by this Court to consider the claim of the petitioners under the land pooling policy if otherwise they fulfill the prescribed norms.

10. Shri Sumit Suri holding brief of Shri Nipun Singh, appearing for the respondent, Parishad, very fairly states that the claim of the petitioners would be considered by the Housing Commissioner in terms of the Board's resolution dated 24.06.2022 taken in 256th meeting of the Board.

11. Accordingly, without expressing any final opinion as to the admissibility of the claims of the petitioners, we dispose of the instant petition with direction to the Housing Commissioner i.e.
respondent No. 2 to consider and decide the claim of the petitioners under the land pooling policy within a period of eight weeks from the date of communication of the instant order along with a fresh representation.

The consideration would be accorded without being influenced by the fact that in terms of order dated 14.03.2023 passed in Writ-C No. 18402 of 2020 and similar orders passed in other connected cases, there was direction to the Special Land Acquisition Officer to determine the compensation amount and declare award.
Order Date :- 10.4.2024
